description: Add scattered seborrheic keratoses on trunk
presentation: A 71-year-old man who is a former smoker with type 2 diabetes and chronic eosinophilia underwent a noncontrast CT chest for lung cancer screening. The CT revealed new tree-in-bud micronodularity in the right lower lobe, along with bronchial wall thickening and mucus plugging, not present on imaging from 5 years prior. He remembers a self-limited cough several weeks ago, has no current respiratory symptoms, and has no other systemic complaints or history of reflux. Physical examination is notable for scattered seborrheic keratoses on the trunk. Is additional follow-up needed?
